newsitem.title: USA: New Mexico to join Powerball as lottery grows.
newsitem.headline: New Mexico to join Powerball as lottery grows.

text.p: Building on the success of its instant-win state lottery, New Mexico is to join the national Powerball lottery game on October 20.

Ralph Decker, chief executive officer of the New Mexico Lottery, said the Powerball game would generate around $26 million in state sales during the lottery's fiscal year 1997, which ends June 30, 1997.
New Mexico launched a scratch-card lottery in April and Decker said it was exceeding expectations on sales and on profit margins.
"We're just real thrilled with the way we started and the way the people accepted this lottery," said Decker.

He said New Mexico Lottery sales, including Powerball and another on-line game called Daily Millions which is to be introduced in February, should reach a total of $95 million in fiscal year 1997, with profits in the region of $21.8 million.
Powerball, an on-line, computerized game, offers jackpots starting at $5 million and reaching as high as $110 million.
New Mexico is the 21st state, including the District of Columbia, to introduce Powerball.
New Mexico state law earmarks 50 percent of lottery profits to public school districts and 40 percent to help college students pay in-state tuition fees.
